title.narrative: Democratic Consolidation and Transformed Local Governance in Ghana

description.narrative:
This engagement was the continuation of a project originally formulated prior to the 2016 elections and since implemented by IDEG with the support of several donors. The project, “Democratic Devolution Strengthens Developmental Governance” (DDSDG) contributed to forging consensus between the two sides in Parliament and to advance the process towards amending the Constitution until the amendment process was suspended in 2019.
The objective of the follow-on engagement was three-fold: to foster peaceful and conducive environment for the 2020 presidential and parliamentary elections, to help IDEG build national consensus around the constitutional reforms and legislative processes for their amendment in place or far advanced and, to strengthen the institutional capacity of IDEG.
The strategic project objective was drawn from IDEG’s overall strategy for Enhanced Democratic Development Strengthens Developmental Governance (DDSDG) (2020 – 2025). The Danish support provided resources to the Institute for Democratic Governance (IDEG)) for the period 2020 – 2022.
The Danish support to IDEG had two components – the first, to influence the resetting of the constitutional amendment agenda and the roadmap for the reform of the hybrid local government system and the second, targeting the elections process in Ghana. The Embassy based its support on progress attained in the implementation of the engagement as described in the documentation provided by IDEG. As part of IDEG’s strategy, in the period 2020 – 2025, IDEG prioritised the implementation of specific projects, which would advance the goal of strengthening democracy, institutions and people-centred development in Ghana and selected African countries.
To facilitate constitutional amendments that will reform Ghana’s hybrid local government system and consolidate democratic stability, peace and security in the Fourth Republic
